word:hebrew:H1003.explanation: This Hebrew word refers to fortresses—strong, defended places built for protection. It functions as a noun describing substantial defensive structures rather than ordinary dwellings. In its two Old Testament occurrences, it is used of fortified construction in 2 Chronicles, and the related wording presents these fortresses as places that were built and became strong. The word’s sense is therefore concrete and architectural: fortified places intended to provide security. Its precise force in either verse depends on the surrounding passage, but “fortresses” captures its established meaning.

word:hebrew:H1216.explanation: This Hebrew word means “swell.” It describes something becoming enlarged or puffed up. In its two Old Testament occurrences, it is used of the condition of clothing and feet during Israel’s wilderness journey, expressing that they became swollen rather than wearing out. The word functions as a verb, describing a change in condition. Its use in both Deuteronomy 8:4 and Nehemiah 9:21 connects the same idea with God’s preservation of Israel’s clothing and feet over forty years.

word:hebrew:H1289.explanation: Berak means to bless and can also mean to kneel.

word:hebrew:H1331.explanation: Bethulim means virginity. It can also refer concretely to tokens of virginity.

word:hebrew:H1393.explanation: Gibʻônîy means a Gibeonite, an inhabitant of Gibeon.

word:hebrew:H1555.explanation: Golyath is a personal name for a Philistine, rendered Goliath in English.

word:hebrew:H1649.explanation: “Gershonites” refers to the people descended from or belonging to Gershon. It functions as a plural group name, identifying a family or clan rather than describing an action or quality. In the Hebrew Old Testament, it occurs 13 times, beginning in Numbers and continuing through Chronicles. The word is especially associated with the Gershonite group among Israel’s families and with their recognized place in the community’s service and organization.

word:hebrew:H1670.explanation: Dᵉʼâbâh means pining; by analogy, it can also mean fear.

word:hebrew:H1753.explanation: Dûwr means to reside or dwell.

word:hebrew:H1784.explanation: Dîynay means a Dinaite, or an inhabitant of an unknown province of Assyria.

word:hebrew:H1836.explanation: Dên means this. It can also refer to a matter or express thus.

word:hebrew:H1890.explanation: Habhâb means a sacrificial gift or offering.

word:hebrew:H1924.explanation: Hadar is a Hebrew personal name, rendered “Hadar,” rather than a common word whose meaning can be defined from the available lexical information. It occurs once in the Hebrew Old Testament, at Genesis 36:39. In that occurrence, Hadar is linked with a recorded death event, but that connection describes the surrounding record rather than establishing an additional meaning for the name. Thus, the supported meaning is simply Hadar.

word:hebrew:H1951.explanation: “Ready” is the supported meaning of this Hebrew word. It serves as an action word, expressing that someone is prepared to act or proceed. The word occurs once in the Hebrew Old Testament, in Deuteronomy 1:41. Because the verse text is not available here, its precise force in that sentence must be understood from the surrounding passage; however, its ordinary lexical sense points to preparedness rather than naming a person, place, or object.

word:hebrew:H2011.explanation: Hinnom is a personal name, apparently that of a Jebusite. It appears in the name “the valley of the son of Hinnom.”

word:hebrew:H2064.explanation: This Hebrew word is a verb that appears once, in Genesis 30:20. Its precise ordinary meaning cannot be stated confidently because no gloss, definition, or approved rendering is attached to it here. The verse reference identifies its only occurrence, while SEE relationships show it functioning as the predicate in that sentence. Understanding its exact sense therefore requires the actual verse wording and surrounding context rather than a guessed translation.

word:hebrew:H2125.explanation: Zizah is a Hebrew personal name, rendered “Zizah” in English. It functions as a name rather than a general description or action word. This name appears once in the Hebrew Old Testament, at 1 Chronicles 23:11. Because no explicit lexical definition is available, the name itself is the clearest supported meaning; its precise significance cannot be expanded beyond identifying the person named in that passage.

word:hebrew:H2222.explanation: Zarzîph means pouring rain and can also refer to water.

word:hebrew:H224.explanation: Urim refers to the bright figures in the high priest’s breastplate, used to seek judgment before Yahweh.

word:hebrew:H2327.explanation: Hobah is a proper place-name in the Hebrew Old Testament. It identifies a location rather than expressing an action, quality, or general idea. The name occurs once, in Genesis 14:15, and the available rendering preserves it as “Hobah.” Because no verse text or broader context is included here, its precise location or significance cannot be described further from this word alone.

word:hebrew:H2378.explanation: This Hebrew word is a rare term whose precise ordinary meaning cannot be established from the available lexical information. It occurs once in the Hebrew Old Testament, at 2 Chronicles 9:29. Its record supplies the Hebrew identity and reference but no explicit definition, rendering, or grammatical description. Therefore, it should not be assigned an English meaning beyond what the surrounding verse and broader scriptural context may establish. The word’s exact role belongs to verse-level study of that passage.

word:hebrew:H2446.explanation: Chakaljah is an Israelite personal name, rendered Hachaliah in English.

word:hebrew:H251.explanation: Ach means brother, including a literal family relationship. It can also mean another, as in a reference to another brother.

word:hebrew:H2688.explanation: This Hebrew word refers to Tamar, a named place. It is not presented as an action, quality, or general object, but as a location identified by name. Within the Hebrew Old Testament corpus, it occurs four times in two verses, with the English rendering Tamar. Its references span Genesis 14:7 and 2 Chronicles 20:2, showing that the name is used in different historical settings while retaining the same place-name function.

word:hebrew:H2723.explanation: Chorbâh means desolation, describing places left waste or ruined.

word:hebrew:H2914.explanation: Techor means a boil or ulcer, especially a tumor in the anal or genital area.

word:hebrew:H3009.explanation: This Hebrew word functions as a predicate associated with the earth, describing something said of it. Its precise lexical meaning cannot be stated more narrowly because no short definition, gloss, or approved meaning candidate is available. It occurs only once in the Hebrew Old Testament corpus, in Jeremiah 52:16. In that occurrence, the word is linked with the earth and several related entities, confirming its role in describing an action or condition connected with the land. The surrounding verse text would be needed to explain its specific sense there.

word:hebrew:H3030.explanation: This Hebrew word is a proper name rendered “Idalah.” It identifies a named person, place, or thing rather than expressing an action, quality, or general idea. The word occurs once in the Hebrew Old Testament, in Joshua 19:15, and both recorded English renderings preserve it as “Idalah.” Because no explicit definition or surrounding verse text is available here, its meaning is best understood as the identity of the named item itself, not as a translatable descriptive term.

word:hebrew:H3096.explanation: Yahats names a place east of the Jordan, appearing in Scripture as Jahaz or Jahazah.

word:hebrew:H3113.explanation: “Joiakim” is a personal name, referring to an individual rather than expressing a general idea or action. In the Hebrew Old Testament, it occurs four times, all in Nehemiah 12. The passages place the name within a priestly genealogy, where family succession and recorded ancestry are being identified. Because it is a proper name, its meaning in a particular verse comes chiefly from identifying which person named Joiakim is being mentioned.

word:hebrew:H3218.explanation: Yeleq means a devourer, specifically a young locust, and is also rendered as a cankerworm.

word:hebrew:H3247.explanation: This Hebrew noun refers to a foundation or the bottom part of something—the supporting base on which something rests. It is used for a physical base, including the bottom of an altar, and can also describe a foundation in a broader sense. The word occurs 20 times in the Hebrew Old Testament, showing use across both worship instructions and other passages that speak of established foundations. Its precise force in a particular verse depends on what structure or thing is being described.

word:hebrew:H3302.explanation: Yaphah means to be beautiful or fair. It can also describe making something beautiful or decking something.

word:hebrew:H336.explanation: ʼîy means not. It can also mean island.

word:hebrew:H3441.explanation: This Hebrew word refers to “Jesuites,” a named group or family designation. It occurs once in the Hebrew Old Testament, in Numbers 26:44. Because the available text does not provide a fuller definition or surrounding verse context, the safest understanding is the name itself rather than an added description of the people or their history. Its meaning is therefore chiefly identifying: it marks the group named Jesuites in that genealogy or census record.

word:hebrew:H3517.explanation: This Hebrew word means “heavily,” describing something done with great weight or difficulty. It appears once in the Old Testament, in Exodus 14:25, and functions as an adverb describing how an action occurs. Its single recorded rendering is consistent, so the central idea is weightiness rather than a separate name, object, or person. The surrounding verse supplies the specific force of the word in that passage.

word:hebrew:H3548.explanation: This Hebrew word means “priest,” referring to a person designated for priestly service before God. It is used throughout the Old Testament for individuals identified as priests, especially in passages involving worship, offerings, sacred responsibilities, and guidance concerning holy matters. The word occurs 750 times in the Hebrew Old Testament, from Genesis through Malachi, showing its broad and established use for this role.

word:hebrew:H3706.explanation: Kᵉʻeneth means “thus” in the formula “and so forth.” It can also mean “at such a time.”

word:hebrew:H3799.explanation: Katham means to mark or inscribe something indelibly. In Scripture, iniquity is marked before Yahweh.

word:hebrew:H3838.explanation: This Hebrew word is a personal name rendered “Lebana” or “Lebanah.” It identifies a person in the Old Testament records of returning families, appearing once in Ezra and once in Nehemiah. Because no short definition or ordinary descriptive meaning is provided, the word should be understood primarily as a name rather than expanded into an unrelated concept. Its precise significance in either passage depends on the surrounding verse and list of names.

word:hebrew:H3867.explanation: Lāvâh means to join or unite. It can also mean to lend. It can also mean to borrow.

word:hebrew:H390.explanation: Accad is a proper name rendered “Accad.” It identifies a specific named entity rather than expressing an action, quality, or general idea. This Hebrew word occurs once in the Hebrew corpus, in Genesis 10:10. Because the available passage text is not included here, its precise role in that verse cannot be described further; however, the repeated rendering supports “Accad” as the word’s ordinary English representation. It functions as a name, not as a common noun or descriptive term.

word:hebrew:H3962.explanation: Lasha is a Hebrew place name, referring to a location rather than describing an action, quality, or person. It appears once in the Hebrew Old Testament, in Genesis 10:19, and is rendered “Lasha” in the available English translations. Because it functions as a proper name, its ordinary role is to identify a particular place. The surrounding verse determines how that location fits into the larger geographic description.

word:hebrew:H4017.explanation: Mibsam is a personal name, functioning as a proper name rather than as a general description or action. It identifies a person in the Hebrew Old Testament and is consistently rendered “Mibsam.” The name occurs three times, in Genesis and 1 Chronicles, so its ordinary sense is the designation of that individual rather than a broader concept. The surrounding verse text would be needed to explain the person’s particular role in each passage.

word:hebrew:H4134.explanation: Mûwk means to become poor or impoverished.

word:hebrew:H4141.explanation: The Hebrew word means “winding.” It describes something that follows a winding course rather than a straight one. It occurs once in the Hebrew Old Testament, in Ezekiel 41:7, so its broader range cannot be established from repeated uses. The word gives a concise description of this quality, while its precise force in that verse depends on the surrounding passage.

word:hebrew:H4206.explanation: Mâzîyach means a movable belt or girdle. In some contexts, it is rendered as strength.

word:hebrew:H4299.explanation: This Hebrew word means “spun”: it describes the action of making thread by twisting fibers together. It occurs once in the Hebrew Old Testament corpus, at Exodus 35:25, and functions as a verb describing work performed on material. The word therefore points to the process of spinning rather than naming the finished thread or the person doing the work. Its precise force in that verse depends on the surrounding wording.

word:hebrew:H4387.explanation: This Hebrew word is a specialized term whose precise meaning cannot be stated confidently from the available lexical information. It appears only once in the Hebrew Old Testament, at Psalm 16:1, and the verse text is not available here to clarify its use. Therefore, it is best treated as an untranslated Hebrew term rather than assigned an invented English meaning.

word:hebrew:H4413.explanation: Mallothi is a personal name, rendered “Mallothi.” It identifies an individual in the Old Testament rather than expressing a general action, quality, or object. The name appears twice, both times in 1 Chronicles 25, and the available wording preserves it as a name instead of translating it into an ordinary English meaning. Its specific role belongs to the surrounding passage, but the word itself functions as a proper name. This Hebrew name is therefore best understood simply as identifying Mallothi.

word:hebrew:H4509.explanation: Miniamin is a personal name, referring to an individual named Miniamin rather than expressing a general idea or action. In the Hebrew Old Testament, the name appears three times: once in 2 Chronicles and twice in Nehemiah. One occurrence is associated with receiving or distributing gifts, but the name itself identifies the person and does not carry a broader meaning in the available passages. It is rendered consistently as “Miniamin.”

word:hebrew:H4530.explanation: “Tribute” is the supported meaning of this Hebrew word. It refers to something given, functioning as the object of giving in its only recorded Hebrew-Bible occurrence. The word appears once, in Deuteronomy 16:10, so its broader range cannot be established from repeated uses. Its association there is with giving, and the wording consistently renders it as “tribute.” The surrounding verse would be needed to explain the specific tribute and its purpose.

word:hebrew:H4596.explanation: Mei means a heap of rubbish or a ruin.

word:hebrew:H4602.explanation: Maachathite means an inhabitant of Maakah.

word:hebrew:H466.explanation: Eliphelehu is the name of an Israelite.

word:hebrew:H4718.explanation: Maqqebeth means a hammer. It can also refer to a quarry.

word:hebrew:H4747.explanation: Mᵉqêrâh means a cooling off, rendered as “summer” in these passages.

word:hebrew:H4835.explanation: Merutsah means oppression and can also refer to violence.

word:hebrew:H5043.explanation: This Hebrew word refers to a “candlestick,” a stand or fixture intended to hold candles and provide light. It occurs once in the Hebrew corpus, at Daniel 5:5. Because no verse text or surrounding context is available here, the word’s basic meaning can be stated, but its precise significance in that scene must be understood from the passage itself and its setting.

word:hebrew:H5094.explanation: Nehir means illumination or light. It can also refer figuratively to wisdom.

word:hebrew:H512.explanation: The word means “Elkoshite,” a designation identifying a person by connection with Elkosh. It functions as a name-like descriptive label rather than an action or quality, marking someone’s association with a place or community. In the Hebrew Old Testament corpus, it occurs once, at Nahum 1:1. The surrounding verse text is needed to explain how the designation functions there in context.

word:hebrew:H5142.explanation: Nezaq means to suffer loss. It can also describe causing damage.

word:hebrew:H5256.explanation: This Hebrew word means “pulled.” It functions as a verb, expressing the action of pulling rather than naming a person, object, or quality. In the Hebrew Old Testament, it occurs once, in Ezra 6:11. The word’s basic sense is therefore concise and action-centered: it identifies something as having been pulled. Its precise role in that verse depends on the surrounding context.

word:hebrew:H5371.explanation: Nergal-Sharetser is the name of two Babylonians.

word:hebrew:H5421.explanation: Natha means to tear out, as of young lions' teeth being broken away.

word:hebrew:H5454.explanation: This Hebrew word is a personal name rendered “Sabta” or “Sabtah.” It identifies the same named person in two Old Testament occurrences: Genesis 10:7 and 1 Chronicles 1:9. The spelling differs slightly between English renderings, but the Hebrew entity is the same. Because no explicit definition is given, the word should be understood as a name rather than as a term describing an action, quality, or idea. Its precise role in either passage depends on the surrounding genealogy and verse context.

word:hebrew:H5537.explanation: Sāla means to suspend something in a balance—to weigh it for comparison.

word:hebrew:H5568.explanation: Samar means to stand up or bristle, as hair does. It can also describe trembling.

word:hebrew:H5645.explanation: ʻAb means a cloud, especially a thick or dense cloud. It can also refer to clay.

word:hebrew:H5700.explanation: Eglon is the name of a place in Palestine.

word:hebrew:H5739.explanation: Eder means a flock, herd, or drove—an organized group of animals.

word:hebrew:H585.explanation: Anachah means sighing or groaning. Scripture renders it as sighing in one passage and as groaning in another passage.

word:hebrew:H5919.explanation: Akshuwb means an asp or adder.

word:hebrew:H5920.explanation: Al means above, high, or on high. It can also refer to God as the Most High.

word:hebrew:H5986.explanation: Amos is a personal name. The name identifies an Israelite prophet whose words concern Israel.

word:hebrew:H6024.explanation: Anab is the name of a place in Palestine.

word:hebrew:H6051.explanation: Anan means a cloud, such as the cloud that covered the mountain.

word:hebrew:H6136.explanation: Iqqar means a stock or stump—the part of a tree left in the ground after the tree is cut down.

word:hebrew:H6190.explanation: This Hebrew noun refers to the “foreskin,” the bodily covering named in passages concerning circumcision and related matters. It occurs 16 times in the Hebrew Old Testament, beginning in Genesis and continuing through Jeremiah. The word identifies a physical body part rather than an action or abstract idea. Its ordinary meaning remains consistent across its occurrences, while the surrounding passage determines the specific instruction or event involving it.

word:hebrew:H6275.explanation: Athaq means to remove or move away. It can also describe becoming old. In another use, it means stopping or ceasing to speak.

word:hebrew:H628.explanation: Aspesuph means a mixed multitude—a gathered-together group of people.

word:hebrew:H6428.explanation: Palash means to roll or wallow in dust.

word:hebrew:H6477.explanation: Petsîyrâh means bluntness in a context where tools are sharpened. It can also refer to a file used to sharpen tools.

word:hebrew:H6550.explanation: “Flea” refers to the insect named by this Hebrew word. It functions as a concrete noun, identifying a creature rather than expressing an action, quality, or abstract idea. The word occurs twice in the Hebrew Old Testament, both times in 1 Samuel, and each occurrence is rendered “flea.” Its precise force in either sentence depends on the surrounding passage, but its basic meaning remains the name of this creature.

word:hebrew:H6666.explanation: Tsedaqah means righteousness or rightness. It can also describe righteous conduct, such as acts identified as righteous.

word:hebrew:H6712.explanation: Tsᵉchôq means laughter. It can describe laughter shared in pleasure or laughter expressed in derision.

word:hebrew:H677.explanation: Etsba means a finger or a toe.

word:hebrew:H6785.explanation: Tsemer means wool. It can refer to wool in clothing or to a fleece of wool.

word:hebrew:H6903.explanation: Qebel means because or on account of. It can also mean therefore, or before and in front of something.

word:hebrew:H7276.explanation: Regem is a Hebrew personal name, rendered as “Regem.” It does not function here as an ordinary descriptive word such as an action, quality, or object; it identifies a person. In the Hebrew Old Testament, this name occurs once, at 1 Chronicles 2:47. Without the verse text and its surrounding passage, the name itself does not provide further information about the person’s character, role, or significance.

word:hebrew:H7333.explanation: Razon means a dignitary, such as a prince.

word:hebrew:H7391.explanation: This Hebrew word means “tenderness.” It names a quality or condition rather than describing an action. In the Hebrew Old Testament, it occurs once, in Deuteronomy 28:56. The English rendering “tenderness” provides the clearest basic sense for understanding the word. Its precise force in that verse depends on the surrounding passage, which is not included here, so the word’s normal lexical meaning is the most certain point available.

word:hebrew:H7438.explanation: Rôn means a shout of deliverance. It can also mean a song of deliverance.

word:hebrew:H7467.explanation: This Hebrew word functions as a personal name, rendered “Reuel.” It identifies people bearing that name rather than describing an action, quality, or object. In the Hebrew Old Testament corpus, it occurs 11 times across 10 verses, including genealogical records and narrative passages. Its use in these settings shows it serves to identify specific individuals. The precise person depends on the surrounding passage, since the name appears in more than one biblical setting.

word:hebrew:H750.explanation: Arēk means long, especially when describing someone who is slow to anger.

word:hebrew:H7562.explanation: Reshaʻ means a wrong, especially a moral wrong. It is expressed as wickedness or iniquity.

word:hebrew:H7665.explanation: Shabar means to burst or break apart.

word:hebrew:H769.explanation: Arnon is the name of a river. It can also refer to the territory associated with that river.

word:hebrew:H7759.explanation: Shulammith is a feminine name or epithet for a woman.

word:hebrew:H7760.explanation: Suwm means to put or set something in place. It can also describe making someone a father or ruler.

word:hebrew:H7834.explanation: Shachaq refers to clouds or the sky.

word:hebrew:H7841.explanation: Shehariah is a personal name, rendered as “Shehariah.” It identifies an individual in the Hebrew Old Testament rather than describing an action, quality, or general idea. This name occurs once, in 1 Chronicles 8:26. The available passage information identifies the person by name but does not provide enough verse text here to explain the name’s deeper significance or the individual’s role. Its ordinary function is therefore simply to designate that person in the genealogy or list where the name appears.

word:hebrew:H7917.explanation: Sekirah means a hiring or something hired.

word:hebrew:H7948.explanation: This Hebrew word refers to “ledges,” meaning raised edges or projecting parts of a structure. It appears three times in the Hebrew Old Testament, all in the description of Solomon’s temple furnishings in 1 Kings 7:28–29. Its repeated rendering as “ledges” gives the clearest ordinary meaning available here. The word describes a physical architectural feature rather than an action, quality, or person. The surrounding verse text would be needed to explain the exact shape or placement of these ledges in each occurrence.

word:hebrew:H8088.explanation: Shema means something heard, including a report.

word:hebrew:H8123.explanation: Shimshon is the name of an Israelite. English translations render the name Samson.

word:hebrew:H8181.explanation: This Hebrew noun means “hair”: the word refers to hair on a person's body or head. Scripture uses it when speaking about physical appearance or what happens to hair. In the Old Testament corpus, it occurs 28 times, with especially frequent use in Leviticus. Its precise force in a particular passage depends on the surrounding sentence, but its ordinary meaning remains hair, not an action or abstract quality.

word:hebrew:H8246.explanation: This Hebrew word refers to an almond or an almond-shaped design. It occurs six times in the Old Testament Hebrew text, all in four passages in Exodus describing the construction of the lampstand and its decorative features. The word is consistently rendered “almond,” so its ordinary sense is tied to the almond form or its representation in the lampstand’s design. Its precise function in each verse depends on the surrounding description, but it belongs to the vocabulary of the lampstand’s crafted ornamentation.

word:hebrew:H831.explanation: Ashkelon is a place in Palestine.

word:hebrew:H8372.explanation: Ta means a room or chamber.

word:hebrew:H8422.explanation: Tubal is a personal name, listed among Japheth’s sons and later used for the people descended from him.

word:hebrew:H844.explanation: Asriel is a personal name, rendered “Asriel,” associated with a person recorded in Israel’s genealogical lists. It appears three times in the Hebrew Old Testament, in Numbers, Joshua, and 1 Chronicles. The surrounding SEE connections place the name in family-line and birth-or-begetting contexts, showing that it identifies an individual within a genealogy rather than expressing an action, quality, or command.

word:hebrew:H8527.explanation: This Hebrew word refers to a “scholar,” identifying a person by that designation. It occurs once in the Hebrew Old Testament corpus, in 1 Chronicles 25:8. Since no verse text or broader lexical definition is available here, “scholar” is the clearest supported ordinary meaning. The word names the person rather than describing an action. Its precise role in that verse depends on the surrounding context, which determines how the designation functions there.

word:hebrew:H8578.explanation: This Hebrew word means “second,” identifying someone or something as next in an ordered sequence. It occurs once in the Hebrew Old Testament corpus, at Daniel 7:5. As an ordinal expression, it marks position rather than describing a person’s character, action, or condition. Its precise significance in that passage depends on the surrounding verse and vision, which are not included here.

word:hebrew:H8611.explanation: Tôpheth means contempt shown by making someone a public byword.

word:hebrew:H8664.explanation: Tishbîy means a Tishbite, an inhabitant of Tishbeh in Gilead.

word:hebrew:H893.explanation: Bebai is the name of an Israelite.

word:hebrew:H916.explanation: Bedolach refers to bdellium, a fragrant gum.

word:hebrew:H989.explanation: Bᵉṭêl means to stop. It can also mean to make people stop or hinder them. It can describe work ceasing as well.
